Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they form the standard loop: (1) pick/build best AUB module candidate, (2) run full system candidate sweep, (3) generate a targeted fix plan based on latest results.

### 1) AUB module autopilot (select best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
What it does:
- Loads module candidates from `module_registry.yaml`
- Runs their evaluations
- Promotes the best-performing module candidate (per your selection criteria) so downstream system runs use it

What to check after:
- A summary table of candidates and metrics (means/mins)
- Whether a new “PASS” candidate is produced (right now you have none)

### 2) System autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
What it does:
- Executes the full system experiments defined in `system_candidates.yaml`
- Produces system-level comparisons vs the current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`)

What to check after:
- Any candidate beating champion on your primary objective (looks like `tuning_mean/min` plus `lockbox_mean/min`)
- Regressions on “min” metrics in particular (your champion has a low tuning_min ~0.43; don’t accidentally optimize mean while harming min)

### 3) Generate the next fix plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What it does:
- Looks at the latest module/system outcomes
- Writes a concrete “next fix” plan to `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` (typically pointing to the weakest metric slices and suggesting which module to modify)

### Practical notes / gotchas
- If your setup uses cached results, consider clearing/isolating the run directory if you suspect stale evaluations.
- If “select-best” chooses based on mean only, but you care strongly about min (seems likely), confirm the selection criterion in the tool/config; otherwise it may pick something that looks good on average but fails worst-case.

If you paste the stdout summaries from commands (1) and (2), I can help interpret whether anything is truly champion-beating and what to change next if everything is still INCONCLUSIVE.
